doc.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Dizzy named chief in Africa
summary: On an Africa tour with Dizzy, Dizzy was made a bashir and slipped the chief gin.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Nine years April the third. We were. And when I left here after playing the two weeks I was here, I was in love when I left, and I didn’t want her to forget me so I had them send her a dozen roses every Monday, see? So I went on tour with Dizzy to Africa, that’s when we went — was it a month, honey? Month and a half? That’s all? Anyway my phone bill was twelve hundred bucks a week.

And they made Dizzy a bashir, a chief, in Africa. It was funny. Because we’re sitting and the tribe is out there and the chief is sitting up on the thing, and so Dizzy gets this hat you know, the bashir and all like that you know, and then I look and he’s slipped the chief a bottle of Gordon gin because the chief liked that. And the chief put his bottle and took a little swig, man, you should have seen the smile on his face. And you know we had to fly on two chartered planes. They were from Gulf Oil. Because the planes over there, man. But that was a hell of an experience boy.
